item.title: [LU-20623] interop sanity test_27D: llapi_layout_test test30 test37 failed
item.description:
This issue was created by maloo for Andreas Dilger <adilger@dilger.ca>

This issue relates to the following test suite run:
https://testing.whamcloud.com/test_sets/c9bc7848-bf26-4926-9303-5bf4bf4d4c10

test_27D failed with the following error:

llapi_layout_test: llapi_layout_test.c:1970: test37: assertion 'rc == 0' failed: errno = 22
 test37 @1787258879: verify mirror count and mirror ids for existing files ..... fail (exit status 1)

Test session details:
clients: https://build.whamcloud.com/job/lustre-master-next/1004 - 5.14.0-687.39.1.el9_8.x86_64
servers: https://build.whamcloud.com/job/lustre-b2_16/6 - 5.14.0-427.31.1_lustre.el9.x86_64

It looks like this started failing on interop testing on both master and master-next since 2026-06-08. It did not fail in the 2026-06-02 or earlier master-next runs (though there were some EC-related interop failures in the 5x range). It looks like these failures are intermittent and exist back to 2026-04-02 but was hidden by other permanent failures in the test5x range.

sanity test_27D - llapi_layout_test failed

comments.comment:
mvef,
It looks like sanity test_27D subsub test37 has started failing in interop testing with master clients and b2_16 servers since 2026-06-08. The verify mirror count and mirror ids for existing files test case was added in patch https://review.whamcloud.com/63484 ("LU-12187 llapi: create arbitrary mirror IDs and validate count") related to the EC mirror binding on 2026-03-09, but it looks like a landing on 2026-06-08 broke it for interop.

The list of patches landed on that day that seem like potential candidates are below. I've removed some that don't seem possible to affect this, and likely the sec/ssk tickets are not the culprit since they are not enabled, but I've left them in:

ec956f2541 LU-19958 sec: update rev ctx at first req with new flavor
682cd06e56 LU-19079 nodemap: allow switch to gss_id nodemap
fb7915fa7f LU-19079 sec: update nodemap membership on flavor change
04aa5e079b LU-8229 ssk: support removing keys from keyring via lgss_sk
a009ec6cc1 LU-8229 ssk: support auth against multiple similar keys
c9b777920f LU-8229 ssk: support adding multiple similar server keys
1277366973 LU-19079 ssk: mount-point specific key
acfe100812 LU-20258 lod: reject EC layouts with k+m > 256 (MDS side)
ca1ebeae4a LU-20258 ec: reject EC layouts with k+m > 256
173d35d9f5 LU-17920 mgs: mgs_modify_param() return -EINVAL on bad param
2f2f7d9f82 LU-19001 osp: fix misplaced unlikely() in opd_gap_count check
314dcc614b LU-11850 obd: fixes for Netlink stats
46bab4a2e9 LU-19921 lmv: move register observer before obd_connect
f5f4792700 LU-18891 llite: allow testing up to 2000-stripe dirs
c02c8c2132 LU-19179 llite: remove kernel specific handling
a9efacc730 LU-20285 llite: identify mmap use case by checking CIT_FAULT
df25b9172c LU-19459 llite: use ATTR_CTIME_SET since v6.17
095fa11ec0 LU-20162 obdclass: pin debugfs entries
4277814428 LU-19531 mdd: limit mdd_is_parent() looping
Oleg said he would let his bots isolate the source of this issue.

Reviewing recent interop test sessions with 2.16 servers, it appears that some test sessions pass test37 and some fail with the "errno = 22 = EINVAL" error. While this subtest was added as part of the EC project, nothing that it is doing appears to be EC-specific, and the failure is on line 1972 (fomerly line 1970):

       rc = llapi_layout_comp_del(filelayout);
       ASSERTF(rc == 0, "errno = %d", errno);

so this seems like a legitimate interop regression for FLR files.
Short of running "llapi_layout_test ... -t37" under GDB in interop mode, I don't see any debugging/logging that is emitted related to the failure.
It looks like the same interop failure is also affecting test30, which is failing on line 1407 (formerly line 1405) with "errno = 22 = EINVAL" calling llapi_layout_comp_del().

It looks like I might have a root cause for this issue. In patch https://review.whamcloud.com/61962 ("LU-12187 llapi: EC layout creation support") landed on 2026-03-31 it added a check in llapi_layout_comp_del() that a data component which has a linked parity component cannot be deleted:

+       if (comp->llc_flags & LCME_FL_PARITY) {
[snip]
+       } else {
+               /* A data comp that is protected by a parity comp can't be
+                * deleted until the parity comp is deleted.
+                */
+               if (comp->llc_mirror_link_id != LLAPI_MIRROR_LINK_NONE) {
+                       errno = EINVAL;
+                       return -1;
+               }
+       }

However, in LU-20718 we see that the lcme_timestamp is not zeroed properly and has random garbage written into it (for a yet unknown reason) in non-EC/non-NOSYNC files. This causes llc_mirror_link_id to randomly be non-zero and the llapi_layout_comp_del() check fails.

Fixing the source of the garbage lcme_timestamp field is the purview of LU-20718, but since those bad timestamps are known to date back to at least 2021 (according to my home filesysem), this is a real interop issue that needs to be fixed.

It looks like the best way to handle this is for the llapi_layout_comp_del() check to be conditional on there actually being an EC component with the matching llc_mirror_link_id, or it will cause 2.18+ clients to be randomly unable to delete existing mirror components with garbage lcme_timestamps, regardless of whether EC is enabled or not.
